title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of the typescript 'Courbes elliptiques : formulaire (d'après J. Tate)'. It is Deligne's formulaire, published in Modular Functions of One Variable IV (LNM 476, 1975), §§1–5. Grothendieck's copy is annotated in blue. The page continues §3, 'Cas où 2 et c4 sont inversibles'.

Setting. Over a base S with 2 invertible, an elliptic curve with invariant differential π can be written y^2 = x^3 + a2 x^2 + a4 x + a6, with π = dx/2y. The only remaining coordinate changes are translations x -> x + r. The page first finishes the claim Δ = 2^4 δ, where δ is the discriminant of the cubic. Since δ is translation invariant, it is enough to check the identity when 3 is invertible and a2 = 0.

Normalisation by d6. Under x -> x + r one finds a2a4 − 9a6 ↦ (a2a4 − 9a6) + 2r(a2^2 − 3a4). In terms of the formulaire's quantities this reads d6 ↦ d6 + r c4. So when c4 is invertible there is exactly one r with d6 = 0, i.e. a2a4 = 9a6. This works even when 3 is not invertible.

Normalised formulas. With a2a4 = 9a6:
- (3.3) −c6 = 2^6(a2^3 − 27a6) and Δ = 2^6(−a2^3 a6 − a4^3 + 54 a6^2).
- (3.4) a2 c4 = −c6/4, a4 c4^2 = −36 Δ, a6 c4^3 = c6 Δ.
These are checked in characteristic 0. There the third identity is the product of the first two, divided by 9 using a2a4 = 9a6.

Consequence (Proposition 3.5). Over Z[1/2], the moduli problem 'genus-one curve + invertible invariant differential + c4 invertible' is representable. It is represented by Spec Z[1/2][a2,a4,a6,(a2^2−3a4)^{−1}]/(a2a4−9a6), with universal curve y^2 = x^3 + a2x^2 + a4x + a6 (and π = dx/2y on the next page).

Role. This is part of the systematic description of the moduli of elliptic curves with a chosen invariant differential, i.e. the rigidification over loci of the stack of elliptic curves. It is background for the Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs and Hasse-invariant (Cartier operation) material of this dossier.
errors: Minor point: the 'verify in characteristic 0' argument for (3.4) tacitly uses that the universal ring Z[1/2][a2,a4,a6]/(a2a4−9a6) (localised) is Z-torsion-free. This holds because a2a4 − 9a6 is primitive and the quotient is a flat domain, so the step is fine but unstated.
The text does not stress that the uniqueness of the translation needs only c4 invertible and not 3 invertible. This follows from the identity d6 ↦ d6 + r·c4; it is implicit but correct.

ideas.what: Normal form of a Weierstrass equation with a1 = a3 = 0, plus the extra normalisation d6 = 0 (a2a4 = 9a6), fixed uniquely when c4 is invertible

deep.surprise_reason: This is Grothendieck's annotated copy of Deligne's typescript 'formulaire d'après Tate', which was published in 1975 (LNM 476). The content is correct, routine and well known. The only archival interest is Grothendieck's marginal blue annotations ('9', 'section e').
transcription_corrections: The marginal '{+?+}' after 'non homogène)' is a blue handwritten mark, probably '9', matching the '{+9+}' on the previous page. It is followed by the blue marginal note 'section e'.
'd_6 = 0 ?' should read 'd_6 = 0 ,' (the comma is a stray typewriter mark).
'(3·1)' in the first line has a handwritten correction to '(3.1)'.
